mainTopic: Testing strange discharges, רבי יהודה and the fish-shaped case, and רבי מאיר's animal-shaped birth learned through a גזירה שוה
overview: The גמרא first explains the משנה's water test for discharges that look like shells or hairs. If they dissolve, they are blood and she is טמאה; if they don't, רבה says they are a separate thing, not blood. A ברייתא tells of two real cases brought to the חכמים in יבנה, and the גמרא adds that the water must be lukewarm. It also brings רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's test of mashing with saliva, and it leaves unresolved (תיקו) whether the soak must last twenty-four hours. Next, the גמרא asks why רבי יהודה doesn't argue about a fish-shaped discharge. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן answer in different ways, and the גמרא ties each answer to a version of רבי יוחנן's view. Finally, שמואל explains that רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped discharge like a birth because the Torah says both man and animals were 'formed' (יצירה). Sea monsters, which were 'created' (בריאה), are not included, because the word 'formed' is free on both sides. This leads to the rules for how free a גזירה שוה must be, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The water test: if they dissolve, she is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule of the משנה: if the discharged items dissolve in water, the woman is טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they dissolved, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the משנה's rule about the water test. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items the woman discharged are dry and solid. If they melt in water, that shows they are really dried blood, so she is טמאה. The גמרא understands this to mean that even dry blood makes a woman טמאה.

phrases.english: If they dissolved, she is impure.
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה, about things like shells or hairs a woman discharged and was told to put in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the משנה's water test as the base text for the next question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Discharged solid items that dissolve in water are blood, and the woman is טמאה. This suggests that dry blood is טמא.

steps.title: Then why not impure even if they don't dissolve?
steps.stepSummary: If dry blood is טמא, the items should make her טמאה even when they don't dissolve. So why test them at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, she should be impure also when they do not dissolve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the water test. If dry blood counts, why does it matter whether the items dissolve?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items are dry either way. If dryness does not stop blood from being טמא, then dissolving or not dissolving should make no difference. The challenge says the water test looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: if so, if that is true

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if dry blood is טמא.

phrases.english: then also when they did not dissolve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for the water test from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The water test in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If dry blood is טמא, the items should be טמא whether or not they dissolve, so the test seems useless.

steps.title: רבה: if they don't dissolve, it isn't blood at all
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that items which do not dissolve are a separate thing of their own, not blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: When they do not dissolve, it is a separate thing of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge. He says the water test is not about wet or dry blood. It tells us whether the item is blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dry blood is still טמא, but only if it really is blood. Real blood dissolves in water. Something that stays solid is a separate thing of its own (בריה בפני עצמה), not blood, so she stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: a separate thing of its own, not blood

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the purpose of the water test: it decides what the item is made of, not whether dry blood counts.

phrases.english: רבה said:
When they did not dissolve —
it is a separate thing of its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the test decides whether the item is blood at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water test seemed to be about whether dry blood counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dry blood is טמא. The test only shows whether the item is blood, and items that don't dissolve are not blood.

steps.title: Do such strange cases really happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether women really discharge things like shells and hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks if the cases in the משנה are real or only made up. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Discharges shaped like shells or hairs sound unusual. The גמרא wants to know if this is a real event in life.

phrases.english: And is there really
a case like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the water test to whether such cases exist at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether women really discharge items like shells or hairs, as the משנה describes.

steps.title: Yes: two real cases brought to יבנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. It brings a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says his father brought two such cases from טבעין to יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. It was taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said, My father brought two cases from טבעין to יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes, it happens, and starts bringing proof from a ברייתא. The two cases come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק saw these cases himself through his father. That shows they are real events, not only ideas.

keyTerms.meaning: brought up, brought before the חכמים

phrases.english: Yes, and indeed it was taught:
רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק said:
My father brought up two incidents
from טבעין to יבנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 and opens the proof from a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, such cases happen, as shown by two real incidents brought to the חכמים in יבנה.

steps.title: First case: a woman who discharged red shells
steps.stepSummary: A woman discharged things like red shells. The doctors said she had a wound inside, and the חכמים ruled to use the water test.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman discharged things like red shells. They asked my father, he asked the חכמים, and they asked the doctors. The doctors said she has a wound in her womb that makes these shells. She should put them in water: if they dissolve, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first real case. It matches the משנה's shells case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doctors explained where the shells come from: a wound inside her. The חכמים still used the water test to check if the shells were blood. This matches the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: she should put them into water

phrases.english: There was an incident with a woman who would discharge
things like red shells,
and they came and asked my father,
and my father asked the Sages,
and the Sages asked the doctors,
and they said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה זוֹ מַכָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ,
phrases.english: This woman has a wound inside her womb,
from which she discharges things like shells.
Let her put them into water;
if they dissolved — she is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה מַפֶּלֶת כְּמִין קְלִיפּוֹת אֲדוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two incidents announced in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's case of discharged shells really happens
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: the first incident from טבעין

steps.title: Second case: a woman who discharged red hairs
steps.stepSummary: A woman discharged things like red hairs. The doctors said she had a growth inside, and again the חכמים ruled to use the water test.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another woman discharged things like red hairs. She asked my father, he asked the חכמים, and they asked the doctors. The doctors said she has a growth in her womb that makes these red hairs. She should put them in water: if they dissolve, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second real case. It matches the משנה's hairs case and finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the doctors gave a body reason, a growth inside her. Again the חכמים used the water test. Two real cases prove that the משנה describes things that really happen.
steps.whatToRemember: Strange discharges like shells or hairs really happen. They are tested in water: if they dissolve they are blood and she is טמאה. If they do not dissolve, רבה says they are a separate thing, not blood.

phrases.english: And again, there was an incident with a woman who would discharge
things like red hairs,
and she came and asked my father,
and my father asked the Sages,
and the Sages asked the doctors,
and they said to them:
She has a mole inside her womb,
from which she discharges things like red hairs.
Let her put them into water;
if they dissolved — she is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה מַפֶּלֶת כְּמִין שְׂעָרוֹת אֲדוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second incident, completing the proof begun in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's case of discharged hairs really happens
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: the second incident from טבעין

steps.title: The water must be lukewarm
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש adds that the water test must be done in lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: And it must be in lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds one detail to the water test the חכמים required: the water has to be lukewarm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps said to put the item in water to see if it dissolves. ריש לקיש makes this exact: cold water is not enough, it must be lukewarm (פושרין). Warm water gives real dried blood a fair chance to dissolve.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
And in lukewarm water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the water test from steps 6-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water test is done in lukewarm water.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the lukewarm water rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says to put the item in water, and lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: She puts it into water, and it must be lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's detail is not only his own idea. A ברייתא teaches the same rule, so his statement now has support from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: She should put it into water

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
She should put it into water, and in lukewarm water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's statement in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that the test needs lukewarm water
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says תטיל למים ובפושרין

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's different test: mashing with saliva
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she mashes the item with saliva on her fingernail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: She mashes it with saliva on top of the fingernail.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion: instead of soaking, she mashes the item with saliva on her fingernail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion checks if the item falls apart in lukewarm water. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל checks by rubbing it with saliva on a fingernail. This sets up the next question: what is the real difference between the two tests?

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She mashes it with saliva
on top of the fingernail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The test is done by mashing the item with saliva on a fingernail.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two tests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between soaking and mashing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two opinions would actually give different results. This sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions want to find out if the item is really blood. The גמרא wants a case where one test says blood and the other says not blood.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two opinions in steps 9-10 differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the soaking test and the mashing test give different results.

steps.title: The difference: an item that breaks only with pressure
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the difference is an item that falls apart only when pressed hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The difference between them is something that can be mashed only by pressing hard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers: the two opinions differ about an item that breaks apart only if you press on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In water, such an item would not dissolve by itself, so by the soaking test it is not blood. With the fingernail test, pressing makes it break apart, so it would count as blood. That is the case where the two tests disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Soaking checks if the item dissolves by itself; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's mashing also counts an item that breaks only under pressure.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Something mashed only by pressing hard
is the difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about an item that breaks apart only when pressed hard.

steps.title: How long must the item soak?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a dried שרץ or נבלה soaks for twenty-four hours; the גמרא asks if the same applies here.
steps.simpleTranslation: There we learned: How long must they soak in lukewarm water? Twenty-four hours. Here, what is the rule? Do we need twenty-four hours, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about soaking a dried שרץ or נבלה for twenty-four hours, then asks if the discharged item also needs that long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases use soaking in lukewarm water as a test. The other משנה gives an exact time, מעת לעת. The גמרא asks whether that time also applies to the blood test, or whether a shorter soak is enough.

phrases.english: There we learned:
How long is their soaking in lukewarm water?
phrases.notes: "Their" means a dried-out שרץ or נבלה, from a משנה later in this מסכת (54b).

phrases.english: A full twenty-four hours.
Here, what is the rule?

phrases.aramaic: מִי בָּעֵינָא מֵעֵת לְעֵת, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Do I need twenty-four hours, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a new question about the lukewarm water test.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the discharged item must soak for twenty-four hours like a dried שרץ or נבלה.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe a hard שרץ or נבלה needs twenty-four hours but soft blood does not; or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שרץ and a נבלה, which are hard, need twenty-four hours, but blood, which is soft, does not. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides of its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: a dried שרץ or נבלה is hard, so it needs a long soak; dried blood is soft, so if it doesn't dissolve sooner it is not blood. Side two: the rule is the same, and blood also gets twenty-four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature whose dead body makes things טמא
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: A creeping creature and a carcass, which are hard —
we need twenty-four hours,
but blood, which is soft — no.
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the softness of blood mean a shorter soak is enough?

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is not resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether blood needs a full twenty-four hours. The word תיקו closes this question without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a discharged item must soak a full מעת לעת is a תיקו, left unresolved.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is "no." It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question of steps 13-14 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is unresolved whether the item must soak for twenty-four hours.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה argue about the fish-like case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a woman who discharges something like fish, and asks why רבי יהודה doesn't argue here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: A woman who discharges something like fish. But let רבי יהודה argue in this case too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and challenges why רבי יהודה is silent here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case of the משנה, a shapeless piece, רבי יהודה says she is טמאה even without blood. The משנה says the fish-like case depends on blood, and רבי יהודה does not argue. The גמרא asks why his view would not apply here as well.

phrases.english: A woman who discharges something like fish.
But let Rabbi Yehuda argue in this case too!
phrases.notes: In the first case of the משנה, a shapeless piece, he says she is טמאה even without blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a fish-like discharge, where רבי יהודה does not argue
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה calls a shapeless piece טמא even without blood, he should say the same about a fish-like item.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is disputed, and the משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that רבי יהודה really does argue about the fish-shaped discharge. The משנה's ruling is the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This case is also a dispute, and the משנה follows the view of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question from step 16. He says רבי יהודה does argue in the fish case too; the משנה simply follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that since רבי יהודה is not mentioned, he must agree. ריש לקיש says that is wrong. The same dispute applies here, but the משנה only quoted the view of the רבנן, so רבי יהודה would rule the woman טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught, stated (here: the case is taught as part of the dispute)
It is the opinion of the Rabbis (the majority view)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
It is taught as a dispute,
phrases.notes: He means the same dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about the piece of tissue applies here too.

phrases.english: and it is the view of the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the משנה follows only one side of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה is not mentioned, he must agree in the fish case
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does argue; the משנה states only the view of the רבנן

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even רבי יהודה agrees here
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can even follow רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only ruled strictly about a piece of tissue, because blood can harden into a piece. Blood cannot harden into the shape of a creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only ruled strictly about a piece of tissue, because blood can congeal and turn into a piece. But blood does not turn into the shape of a creature.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He says רבי יהודה agrees here, because the fish case is different from the piece-of-tissue case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה made the woman טמאה with a חתיכה because the piece itself may just be hardened blood. A shape like a fish or a grasshopper is not something blood turns into. So here there is no reason to treat it as blood, and even רבי יהודה agrees she is טהורה unless blood comes out with it.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the ruling fits this opinion too)
He only said his view up to here; he did not say it in the other case
A piece of tissue with no clear shape
A creature; something with a clear form

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear line between a shapeless piece, which could be hardened blood, and a shaped form, which could not.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said his view there
regarding a piece of tissue,
because blood tends to harden and become a piece,
but a creature, it does not become.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the step 16 question that disagrees with ריש לקיש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's strict ruling about a חתיכה should also apply to a shaped creature
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a shapeless piece could be hardened blood; a creature's shape could not, so even רבי יהודה agrees

steps.title: Challenge from the other version of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: There is a version in which רבי יוחנן said the dispute is about whether the womb can open without blood. If so, רבי יהודה should argue here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to that version where רבי יוחנן said they disagree about whether the womb can open without blood, רבי יהודה should argue in this case too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer by pointing to another version of his own view from earlier (21b).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that version, רבי יהודה's reason is that the womb never opens without some blood coming out. That reason has nothing to do with what the discharge looks like. Any discharge opens the womb, so a fish-shaped one should also make her טמאה according to רבי יהודה, and the distinction from step 18 falls apart.

phrases.english: And according to that version
in which Rabbi Yochanan said

phrases.aramaic: בְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִפְתִיחַת הַקֶּבֶר בְּלֹא דָּם קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: that they disagree about whether the womb can open without blood,
let Rabbi Yehuda disagree in this case too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהודה agrees in the fish case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה's reason is that the womb cannot open without blood, the shape of the discharge does not matter. So he should rule the woman טמאה here too.

steps.title: That version's holders say both אמוראים agree it is disputed
steps.stepSummary: Whoever teaches that version of רבי יוחנן also teaches that here רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say the case is disputed, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches that version teaches it like this: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say this case is disputed, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions go together. Whoever holds the 'womb opening' version also holds that רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רבי יוחנן's answer in step 18 is only according to the other version of his opinion. According to the 'womb opening' version, רבי יהודה does argue in the fish case. There is no contradiction, because each version is consistent with itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches (a certain version)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two consistent pictures of רבי יוחנן. In one, רבי יהודה agrees in the fish case because blood cannot form a creature. In the other, רבי יהודה argues because the womb never opens without blood, and both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יוחנן changed his mind. It means each version of his opinion comes with its own matching ruling here.

phrases.english: The one who teaches that version
teaches it like this:
Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
both say:
It is taught as a dispute, and it is the view of the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָךְ לִישָּׁנָא, מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the versions: each version of רבי יוחנן comes with its own ruling here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's answer in step 18 conflicts with the 'womb opening' version of his view
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the 'womb opening' version, רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש that the case is disputed and the משנה follows the רבנן

steps.title: New משנה line: a discharge shaped like an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: a woman who discharges something shaped like an animal, etc.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges something like a kind of animal, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה. This step sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the fish case, the משנה says (according to רבי מאיר) that an animal-shaped discharge counts as a birth. She keeps the days of טומאה and טהרה of a woman who gave birth, based on whether it is male or female. The גמרא is about to analyze this.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries or discharges something
Like a type of, in the form of
Etc. (the rest of the משנה line)

phrases.english: A woman who discharges something like a kind of animal, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the fish discussion and opens the next part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who discharges something in the form of an animal is treated as having given birth (according to רבי מאיר)

steps.title: The source for רבי מאיר: animals were 'formed' like man
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that רבי מאיר makes the woman טמאה לידה for an animal-shaped fetus because the Torah uses the word יצירה (formation) for animals, just as it does for man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Since the Torah uses the word 'formed' for animals, the same way it does for man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה that was just quoted. That ruling says a woman who discharges an animal-shaped fetus is treated like a woman who gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says that ה׳ 'formed' (וייצר) man, and it also says that He 'formed' the animals. Because the same word appears in both places, רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped fetus like a human birth for the laws of טומאת לידה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole section that follows tests how far this word-link can stretch.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?
Since 'formation' is said about it, just as about man.
phrases.notes: The two verses are בראשית 2:19 (animals were formed) and בראשית 2:7 (man was formed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's ruling comes from the shared word יצירה, which the Torah uses for both man and animals.

steps.title: Challenge: then a sea-monster shape should count too
steps.stepSummary: If a shared creation word is enough, a woman who discharges a sea-monster shape should also be טמאה לידה, because the Torah says ה׳ 'created' the great sea monsters.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a woman who discharges something shaped like a sea monster should be impure as a woman after birth, since 'formation' is said about it as about man, as it says: 'And God created the great sea monsters.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reason by pushing it further. If the shared word works for animals, it should also work for a sea monster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah also describes the sea monsters as made by ה׳ (ויברא, 'created'). If the creation wording is what links an animal to man, then a sea-monster shape should also give טומאת לידה, and that sounds like too much.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, from now on; it introduces a challenge that pushes an idea to an extreme
Sea monster; a large sea creature
Impure with the impurity of a woman after birth

phrases.english: But if so,
a woman who discharges the form of a sea monster,
its mother should be impure as after birth,
since 'formation' is said about it, as about man,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'it is said.'

phrases.english: as it says: 'And God created'
the great sea monsters'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's word-link by stretching it to a case that seems unacceptable.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation of רבי מאיר in step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sea monsters were also made by ה׳ according to the Torah, so the same logic would make a sea-monster shape cause טומאת לידה.

steps.title: Answer: 'formed' links to 'formed,' but 'created' does not
steps.stepSummary: We may compare יצירה with יצירה, but we may not compare בריאה (creation) with יצירה. The sea monsters were 'created,' not 'formed,' so they are not linked to man.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: We learn 'formation' from 'formation,' but we do not learn 'creation' from 'formation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that the sea-monster verse uses a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Man and animals share the exact word 'formed' (וייצר). The sea monsters are described with 'created' (ויברא). The link only works when the same word appears in both places, so the sea monster is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive one case from another
A link between two places in the Torah that use a matching word

phrases.english: They say: We learn 'formation' from 'formation,'
but we do not learn 'creation' from 'formation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sea-monster challenge from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the wording: the verse uses a different word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any Torah word describing how a creature was made links it to man.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the identical word יצירה creates the link. The sea monsters' word is בריאה, so it does not.

steps.title: Challenge: different words with the same meaning can still be linked
steps.stepSummary: Why should a different word matter? The school of רבי ישמעאל links 'the כהן shall return' with 'the כהן shall come,' treating שיבה and ביאה as the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And the priest shall return,' 'And the priest shall come.' This returning is this coming!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave by showing a case where two different words were still linked. The next step adds a second challenge, and steps 27–29 answer them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said the link needs the identical word. But the school of רבי ישמעאל linked שיבה ('return') with ביאה ('come') because they mean the same thing. If so, 'created' and 'formed' should also be linkable, and the sea-monster problem comes back.
steps.confusionAlert: This step only raises a challenge to the rule of step 24. Steps 27–29 answer it by asking which word is free (מופנה).

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return,' 'And the priest shall come':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and ויקרא 14:44. Both verses are about a כהן checking a house for צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 24 that only the identical word can be linked.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 24: 'we do not learn בריאה from יצירה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The school of רבי ישמעאל links different words with the same meaning (שיבה and ביאה). So 'created' and 'formed' should be linkable too.

steps.title: Man is also 'created,' so sea monsters should link to man too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second challenge: the Torah uses בריאה for man too, so we should be able to link sea monsters to man through בריאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, let us learn 'creation' from 'creation,' since it is written: 'And God created man in His image.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another challenge to the answer from step 24. Even if we only compare matching words, man is also described with the word 'created,' just like the sea monsters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said sea monsters are 'created' while man is 'formed,' so the words don't match. But the Torah also says ה׳ 'created' man in בראשית 1:27. So a matching-word link (בריאה to בריאה) between sea monsters and man exists after all, and a sea-monster-shaped fetus should make the woman טמאה לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Creation; the word used for both the sea monsters and man
Let us learn (one case from another)
A link between two topics learned from the same word appearing in both

phrases.english: And furthermore, let us learn 'creation' from 'creation,'
as it is written: 'And God created man in His image'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger challenge to the תירוץ of step 24, alongside the challenge of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that sea monsters (בריאה) cannot be linked to man (יצירה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Man is described with בריאה too, so a matching-word link between sea monsters and man exists, and sea-monster shapes should be included.

steps.title: Only the word 'formed' is extra and free for learning
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'created' is needed to teach about man's creation itself, while 'formed' is extra and free, so only יצירה can be used for a link.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: 'And He created' is needed for its own point; 'And He formed' is free for learning; and we learn 'formation' from 'formation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that not every repeated word can be used for a link. Only a word that is extra in its place can, and here that word is 'formed,' not 'created.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about man being 'created' is needed to tell us that ה׳ made man. The second verse saying man was 'formed' is extra, so it is 'free' to teach a link. That is why animals ('formed') link to man, but sea monsters ('created') do not.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake; needed to teach its own plain point
To be free; extra in its place so it can be used for a link
Formation; the word used for man and for animals

phrases.english: They say: 'And He created' is for its own point,
'And He formed' is to be free,
phrases.notes: The extra verse about man being 'formed' is בראשית 2:7.

phrases.english: and we learn 'formation' from 'formation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which word can be used for a link: only an extra (free) word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any word appearing in both places, like בריאה, creates a link.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the free word, ויצר, creates the link, so animals are linked to man but sea monsters are not.

steps.title: Maybe it is the other way around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: why not say 'formed' is needed for its own point and 'created' is the free one?
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: 'And He formed' is for its own point, 'And He created' is free, and we learn 'creation' from 'creation'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by flipping it. Who says 'formed' is the extra word? Maybe 'created' is the extra one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Man is described with both words, so either one could be the 'needed' one and the other the 'extra' one. If 'created' is the extra word, then sea monsters would be linked to man instead of animals. Step 27 gave no reason to choose one over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite argument is just as good

phrases.english: On the contrary: 'And He formed' is for its own point,
'And He created' is to be free,
and we learn 'creation' from 'creation'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 27 by reversing it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 27 that ויצר is the free word and ויברא is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both words appear about man, so there is no reason to decide that ויצר is the extra one; the reverse is equally possible.

steps.title: 'Formed' is free on both sides, 'created' only on one
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: ויצר is free both in the verse about man and in the verse about animals, while ויברא is free only about man and not about sea monsters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'And He formed' is free on both sides, free regarding man and free regarding animals. 'And He created' is free regarding man, but regarding sea monsters it is not free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that decides between the two words. It looks at whether the word is extra in both verses being linked, not just in man's verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For animals, the word 'formed' is extra in their verse too, so the link is free on both sides. For sea monsters, 'created' is needed in their own verse, so the link is free only on man's side. A link that is free on both sides is stronger, so animals win and sea monsters are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Free on both sides; the linking word is extra in both verses
Sea monsters, which the Torah says ה׳ 'created'

steps.whatToRemember: An animal-shaped fetus is linked to man because ויצר is free in both verses. A sea-monster shape is not, because ויברא is free only on man's side.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the point is that sea monsters lack a matching word. They do share בריאה with man; the difference is that this link is free on only one side, which is weaker.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי מאיר includes animal shapes but not sea-monster shapes for טומאת לידה, and it shows that a link free on both sides beats a link free on only one side.

phrases.english: Rather: 'And He formed' is free on both sides,
free regarding man
and free regarding animals,
phrases.notes: The verse about animals being 'formed' is בראשית 2:19.

phrases.english: 'And He created' regarding man is free,
regarding sea monsters it is not free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by replacing step 27's answer with a stronger reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Compares the strength of the two links: free on both sides versus free on one side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either ויצר or ויברא could be the free word about man, so both links seem equally good.
steps.terutzMaskana: ויצר is free on both sides, ויברא only on one, so the link of animals to man is stronger and is the one we use.

steps.title: Why is the animal word free but not the sea monster word?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ויצר counts as free in the verse about animals. If the reason is that animals were already described earlier, then ויברא about sea monsters should also be free, since 'every creeping thing' already covered them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes the word 'formed' free about animals? If you say it is because the Torah already wrote 'God made the animals of the earth,' and then wrote again 'God formed from the ground every animal of the field,' then the sea monster word should be free too. The Torah wrote 'and every creeping thing of the ground,' and it also wrote 'God created the great sea monsters'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 29, which said ויצר is free about animals and ויברא is not free about sea monsters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word is 'free' (מופנה) when the Torah repeats a fact it already told us, so the word is left over to teach something else. Animals' creation appears twice, so ויצר in the second verse is extra. The challenge says sea monsters also appear twice: once in 'created the great sea monsters' and once inside 'every creeping thing.' If so, ויברא should be free about sea monsters as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, left over: a word not needed for its plain meaning, so it can be used for a גזירה שוה
It is truly free (an emphatic way of saying it)
Sea monster, a large sea creature
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be challenged)

phrases.english: What is 'free' regarding animals?
If you say it is because it is written
"And God made the animals of the earth,"
and it is written "And [ה׳] God formed
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: from the ground every animal of the field,"
then regarding the sea monster too, the word is free,
as it is written "and every creeping thing of the ground,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:25. The questioner assumes this phrase includes sea monsters.

phrases.english: and it is written "And God created the great sea monsters"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 29 that ויברא is not free about sea monsters
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ויצר is free on both sides but ויברא is free on only one side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'double mention' reasoning that makes ויצר free about animals should make ויברא free about sea monsters

steps.title: The creeping things there are land creatures
steps.stepSummary: The 'creeping things' in that verse live on dry land, so they do not include sea monsters. That means the sea monster verse is still needed and its word is not free.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'creeping thing' written there means creatures of the dry land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: 'every creeping thing of the ground' does not include sea monsters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse itself says 'of the ground' (הָאֲדָמָה), so it means land creatures. Sea monsters are therefore mentioned only once, in 'God created the great sea monsters.' That word ויברא is needed to tell us about them, so it is not free on the sea monster side.

phrases.english: The "creeping thing" written there
is of the dry land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the meaning of a verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Every creeping thing' includes sea monsters, so ויברא about them is extra
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Creeping thing' means land creatures only, so ויברא about sea monsters is needed and not free

steps.title: Does it matter if the link is free on one side or both?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between a גזירה שוה that is free on one side and one that is free on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference is there between a word that is free on one side and a word that is free on both sides?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has explained why ויצר is free on both sides, it asks why that matters at all. It is setting up the next step, which brings a rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 29 to 31 worked hard to prove that ויצר is free on both sides and ויברא only on one. The גמרא now wants to know what difference this makes in practice. In other words, why can we not learn just as well from a word that is free on only one side?

keyTerms.meaning: On one side (in only one of the two verses)
On both sides (in both verses of the link)

phrases.english: And what is the practical difference
between a word free on one side
and a word free on both sides?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the distinction proven in steps 29 to 31 matters
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between one-sided and two-sided freedom in a גזירה שוה

steps.title: The rule for how free a גזירה שוה must be
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל in the name of רבי ישמעאל. If a גזירה שוה is not free at all, we cannot learn from it. If it is free on one side, רבי ישמעאל says we learn from it and cannot refute it, while רבנן say we learn from it but can refute it. If it is free on both sides, everyone agrees we learn from it and cannot refute it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference comes from what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, in the name of רבי ישמעאל. Any גזירה שוה that is not free at all cannot be used to learn anything. If it is free on one side, רבי ישמעאל says we learn from it and cannot argue against it, and רבנן say we learn from it but can argue against it. If it is free on both sides, everyone agrees that we learn from it and cannot argue against it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a three-level rule. The rule shows that a link free on both sides is the strongest kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. A link that is not free at all is too weak to use. A link free on one side is in dispute: according to רבנן, a logical difference between the two cases can knock it down. A link free on both sides is so strong that no one can knock it down. So for רבנן, proving 'both sides' protects the link from being refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two verses that use the same word, so a law in one applies to the other
We learn from it (the link is valid)
We refute it, by pointing out a logical difference between the two cases

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of a גזירה שוה. Not free at all means we cannot learn from it. Free on one side is a dispute: we learn from it, but רבנן allow a refutation. Free on both sides means we learn from it with no refutation, according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: משיבין does not mean we never learn from the link. It means that even though we normally learn from it, a strong logical difference between the cases can cancel it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא worked so hard to show that ויצר is free on both sides. A link free on both sides cannot be argued away, even according to רבנן.

phrases.english: The difference is
in what רב יהודה said that שמואל said
in the name of רבי ישמעאל:
Any גזירה שוה
that is not free at all,
we do not learn from it.
If it is free on one side,
according to רבי ישמעאל, we learn from it and do not refute it;
according to רבנן, we learn from it, but we can refute it.
If it is free on both sides,
everyone agrees: we learn from it and do not refute it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבנן, a link free on one side can be refuted, while a link free on both sides cannot be refuted by anyone

steps.title: What difference does it make for רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי ישמעאל, both a one-sided link and a two-sided link can be used and cannot be refuted. So what difference is there for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי ישמעאל, what difference is there between a word free on one side and a word free on both sides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the rule just given shows no difference for רבי ישמעאל. It asks what the difference would be in his view, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the rule, רבי ישמעאל says 'we learn and do not refute' for one-sided links. That is the same result as for two-sided links. So in his view the distinction seems to make no difference.

phrases.english: And according to רבי ישמעאל,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין מוּפְנָה מִצַּד אֶחָד
phrases.english: what difference is there between a word free on one side
and a word free on both sides?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 33, which showed no difference in רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference, according to רבי ישמעאל, between a one-sided link and a two-sided link

steps.title: When two links compete, the stronger one wins
steps.stepSummary: The difference for רבי ישמעאל appears when a one-sided link and a two-sided link point in different directions. In that case we drop the one-sided link.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is in a case where there is a link free on one side and a link free on both sides. Then we let go of the link that is free on only one side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי ישמעאל the difference shows up when two links clash. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי ישמעאל uses both kinds of links, they are not equally strong. If they lead to opposite results, the two-sided link wins and we set the one-sided link aside. In our case, the ויצר link (free on both sides) beats the ויברא link (free on one side).
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, a link free on both sides is stronger. When it clashes with a link free on one side, we follow the two-sided link.

phrases.english: The difference is
that where there is a link free on one side
and a link free on both sides,
we leave aside the link free on one side

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When a one-sided link and a two-sided link clash, the two-sided link wins
